Itinerant

eye-TIN-er-unt · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Itinerant is traveling from place to place, especially for work; having no fixed home.

Before radio and television, itinerant storytellers and musicians traveled between villages, bringing news and entertainment wherever they went.

Worked Example

The itinerant salesman visited a different small town almost every day, never spending more than one night in the same hotel.

Itinerant describes someone who travels from place to place, usually for work, without a fixed permanent home -- here, the salesman's job kept him constantly on the move.

How Itinerant Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

wandering

wandering: moving from place to place without a fixed destination

nomadic

nomadic: having no permanent home, moving from place to place

Antonyms

settled

settled: established permanently in one place

stationary

stationary: not moving; fixed in one place

How Strong Is It? — mobile → itinerant → rootless

mobile vs. itinerant

mobile vs. itinerant: Something mobile is simply capable of moving, without itinerant's specific sense of a repeated, work-driven lifestyle on the road.

rootless vs. itinerant

rootless vs. itinerant: Someone rootless has absolutely no fixed home or attachment anywhere at all, an even more extreme sense of constant movement than itinerant.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of itinerant.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — itiner-

root — itiner-: journey, road, route (Latin iter, itineris)

suffix — -ant

suffix — -ant: characterized by, performing an action (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Itinerant comes from Latin iter, itineris ('a journey, a road'), plus the suffix -ant. Someone itinerant is, quite literally, characterized by constant journeying. The same root gives us the very useful everyday word itinerary -- a planned route or schedule for a journey.

Use the root in a new word: itinerary

Use the root in a new word: itinerary: Before the trip, she printed out a detailed itinerary listing every flight, hotel, and museum visit.

Root Check

Word Choice

Itinerant almost always describes someone's job or lifestyle -- itinerant workers, preachers, musicians, traders -- rather than a single short trip.
